scope: Bounded, read-only static investigation of the three packaged Vulkan-wrapper payloads in app/src/main/assets/graphics_driver/, the upstream v0.0.5r5 release source tag, and the retained upstream Termux build/packaging recipe. Verifies payload identities, attempts a source build into scratch with the recorded local toolchain and an upstream-recipe-aligned relink, and states exactly what is and is not established about default/GameNative source identity. No execution, no device, no packaging or default changes, no upstream submission.
method: Static ELF analysis with Android NDK llvm-readelf/llvm-nm/llvm-strings (NDK 27.3.13750724); hashes with sha256/sha1; GitHub release/tree metadata from retained JSON records and fresh read-only API/archive fetches; one clean scratch build of the verified tag source plus one relink with upstream-aligned link flags. No payload was executed and no emulator/GPU was involved.

verdict.closest_match: Attempt A/B: a library built from the verified v0.0.5r5 tag tree that matches the release payload's SONAME, its 20-name NEEDED set, its wrapper+SPIRV-Tools exported symbol family, and (in attempt B) its 4 KB PT_LOAD alignment and NEEDED link order. The 2.0 MB stripped-size difference and the SPIRV-Tools symbol-set delta remain.
why_not_byte_identical: The release used NDK r27c (27.2.12479018); only r27d (27.3.13750724) is installed, which changes codegen and the embedded .note.android.ident (r27c/API26 vs r27d/API34).

The SPIRV-Tools fork revision built into the release is not recorded in the retained recipe or tag source (empty SPIRV-Tools submodule; empty lib/ directory). The retained pinned archive is the 2026-10-18 revision, which adds 490 exported SPIRV-Tools symbols relative to the release payload.

The release was built inside the Termux package-builder Docker image against a Termux prefix sysroot; the retained local sysroot is a later Wine-experiment Termux fs, so dependency library bytes/versions and link order differ.

Build paths embedded at release time (e.g. /home/Code/mesa/build-wrapper in other upstream artifacts) differ from the scratch build directory; the release is stripped (no .comment) while this rebuild's strip step leaves .ARM.attributes and a TLS .tbss section.
The retained upstream wrapper/ directory only contains 2025-08-20 pre-r5 build outputs, not the r5 build output, so the release link step itself cannot be replayed from retained bytes.

confirmed: All three packaged usr/lib/libvulkan_wrapper.so payloads match the sizes/SHA-256 recorded in docs/PROVENANCE.md; extracted archive bytes and their supporting files are enumerated above.
The packaged wrapper-leegao payload is byte-identical to the official v0.0.5r5 release asset (size 8,709,528; local sha256 520ec0ba...; published GitHub asset digest 520ec0ba...).

The five supporting hook/adrenotools libraries and the ICD JSON in wrapper-leegao.tzst are byte-identical to the upstream Termux packaging repo's retained wrapper/usr/ files, and differ from the supporting files in wrapper.tzst/wrapper-gamenative.tzst; those latter files are identical between the two WinNative archives and equal the local build's hooks/ link inputs.

The downloaded tag archive is the recorded tag tree c8baafbd: 10,336 regular-file blobs and 13 symlinks match the retained tree.json exactly, the 15 CSV files differ only by the archive's *.csv eol=crlf conversion, and no tree blob is missing.
The v0.0.5r5 tag tree contains no .github/workflows or any release workflow; its CI files are upstream Mesa .gitlab-ci. The release recipe is not defined by the tag source.

The upstream release recipe is retained in leegao/vulkan_wrapper_termux-packages (head c5c45d88, 2025-08-20): Termux package build in Docker with NDK r27c, TERMUX_PKG_API_LEVEL=26, --buildtype=release, LDFLAGS -landroid-shmem -ladrenotools, and a zstd/tar .tzst packaging step.

Building the verified tag source with the recorded local recipe succeeds and produces a library with the same SONAME, the same 20-name NEEDED set, and the same wrapper+SPIRV-Tools export family as the release payload; dropping the local 16 KB page-size link flags reproduces the release payload's 4 KB PT_LOAD alignment, and link order -landroid-shmem -ladrenotools reproduces its first two NEEDED entries.

Static fingerprints of the Leegao payload match the retained upstream Termux recipe rather than the recorded local recipe: NDK r27c in .note.android.ident, API level 26, RUNPATH /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/lib:$ORIGIN/../../android_stub, 4 KB PT_LOAD alignment, no .comment, and the termux-prefix link order. The recorded local recipe differs on every one of these (NDK r27d, API 34, build-tree RUNPATH, 16 KB alignment, .comment retained).

The default and GameNative payloads are demonstrably not builds of the v0.0.5r5 source: both are NDK r29/clang 21.0.0 builds with 16 KB alignment and an ICD-only 15-symbol export surface; default embeds debug info and the build directory /data/data/com.termux/files/home/Code/mesa/build-wrapper; both contain code strings (/system/lib64/libgraphicsenv.so, BCn emulation messages, default's graphicsenv_hook.cpp/spirv_patcher.cpp/wrapper_bcdec.c compile units, GameNative's WRAPPER_DIAG marker) that are absent from the tag tree, from commit 3abf4870, and from every upstream branch behind the published head; neither embeds the 24.2.5 Mesa-base string that both known wrapper-branch builds do.

The previous local baseline/candidate builds (3abf4870, recorded recipe) and the tag-source rebuild have byte-identical exported-symbol sets (4073 symbols, sha256 d49d5d70...); the release payload's different export count (3583) is confined to SPIRV-Tools C++ symbols, i.e. a dependency-revision delta rather than a wrapper entrypoint-surface delta.
open: Exact byte reproduction of the v0.0.5r5 release binary from source: not achieved, and not achievable from the retained inputs because NDK r27c, the release-time Termux sysroot/Docker image, the release-time SPIRV-Tools fork revision and the release working tree are not retained.
Source identity of the default payload: not established. It is a different, later wrapper source line built with NDK r29 at a Termux build directory, and its exact revision is not identified.
Source identity of the GameNative payload: not established. It is a different build with NDK r29, a GameNative-specific configuration/marker, and its exact source revision is not identified.

Whether the default/GameNative wrapper sources correspond to a public revision anywhere (all 16 upstream branches plus the two known wrapper-branch commits were checked for the embedded source file names; no match).

The release packaging step that removes .comment/.ARM.attributes and avoids the TLS .tbss section is not reproduced by llvm-strip --strip-all in this environment; the exact strip/elf-cleaner invocation used for the release is not retained.

Whether the uncommitted mesa_bionic working tree built for v0.0.5r5 is byte-identical to tag c8baafbd is not proven (the tag source is the published equivalent; only the four reviewed files were previously checked against the October 2026 source).

what_static_evidence_does_not_establish: It does not prove the release build is deterministic or that any rebuilt binary would match byte-for-byte.
It does not establish the source identity of the default or GameNative wrapper libraries; their archives' supporting files only show shared WinNative packaging lineage.
It does not establish GPU loading, driver initialization, Vulkan conformance, rendering correctness or 16 KB device execution for any payload.
File sizes and symbol counts say nothing about runtime performance, memory use or speed.
limitations: Static analysis only; no payload was executed, no Vulkan loader/driver was involved, no GPU or emulator run.
No device attached; no APK rebuild; no asset/default/packaging change; nothing committed, pushed or submitted upstream.
GitHub metadata was sampled read-only on 2026-10-21; upstream branches/releases may change later.
The .orig/.pb upstream development artifacts in the retained recipe repo are truncated ELF files and could only be fingerprinted through strings and loadable segments, not fully parsed.
